interactions.prompt: i have finished the unet part and now i need to integrate everything into our webots project. can you help me go through the code and figure out how the semantic segmentation, lane detection, object detection, object tracking and traffic detection should work together in the controller? i also need help debugging the webots controller when it crashes and checking whether the python environment and dependencies are correct. when i get errors i will send you the output and can you help me work out what is actually causing it. i also need to make sure my changes are pushed to the correct github branch without overwriting the teams existing files or model
interactions.response:
The different perception components can be integrated into the Webots controller as separate modules while keeping the driving logic centred around lane detection and path following. The semantic segmentation model can load the trained U-Net checkpoint and perform inference on the Webots camera image during runtime. Object detection, object tracking and traffic detection can run alongside it at suitable intervals rather than necessarily being used for steering on every frame.

The controller should keep the interfaces between the modules clear. For example, the segmentation module can return a SegmentationResult containing the predicted segmentation map, while the lane detector can return the lane information required by the path-following and steering controllers.

For debugging, it is useful to separate problems into the repository, Python environment, dependencies, model loading and Webots runtime. Git status, branch information and commit history can be checked first to make sure the correct version of the code is being executed. Python dependencies can then be tested independently before running the complete Webots simulation. Neural-network models can also be loaded individually to determine whether a crash is caused by model initialisation or by the controller itself. For the Git workflow, changes should be made on the appropriate branch, tested locally and then committed and pushed. When integrating the semantic segmentation work with the team code, existing model files should be preserved and the new segmentation model should be added separately. Dependency changes should be recorded in the project configuration so that other team members can install the required packages.

metaReflection.processEvolution: At the start i was asking AI general questions about how the different parts of the project should fit together. As the project got bigger my prompts became much more specific. I started giving AI the actual error messages, git output and webots console output and asking it to help me find the cause. I also started checking individual parts separately, like loading each model, instead of trying to debug the whole controller at once. Towards the end i was using AI more as a debugging and code review tool rather than just asking it to write code.
metaReflection.criticalMoment: One important moment was when my local project seemed different from the github version. I did not just assume that the files were different. I checked the branch, commit hash and remote branch and found that my main branch was pointing to the same commit as origin/main. I also found that webots could modify the .city.wbproj file locally, which explained some of the changes i was seeing. Another important check was when uv installed a CPU only version of pytorch even though my computer has an RTX 3050. I checked the actual pytorch version and cuda availability myself instead of assuming the environment was the same as before.
metaReflection.skillDependency: Without AI the hardest part would have been debugging the interaction between github, uv, python, pytorch and webots because there were several different possible causes for the problems. Understanding the existing code structure and how the different perception modules connected to the controller would also have taken much longer. I could write and change the code myself, but having AI help me interpret error messages and suggest what to test next made the debugging process much faster.
metaReflection.synthesis: I learned that getting the code to work was not just about writing the individual modules. The different parts had to work together with the correct interfaces, dependencies and runtime environment. I also learned a lot about debugging systematically instead of changing random parts of the code when something crashes. AI was useful for explaining errors, suggesting tests and helping me work through the github and webots problems, but the actual verification came from running the tests, checking the terminal output and running the simulation myself.
